newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - U.S. crude build greeted with skepticism.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - U.S. crude build greeted with skepticism.

text.p: A report of a massive build up of crude oil stocks on hand at U.S. refineries was greeted with skepticism by analysts on Tuesday, who attributed the increased inventories in large part to delays in posting import shipments over the past two weeks.

Joe Lastelic, an analyst with the Washington, D.C.-based American Petroleum Institute, said a 10.4 million barrel crude build -- the largest in more than a year -- reflected in large part the timing of tanker arrivals at ports in the Gulf and West coasts.

"I wouldn't be too worked up about that because you could have three ships arrive at the same time, or nine ships instead of the usual six in a week," he said. "It's just the timing" of the arrivals, he said.
The industry trade group in its weekly stocks survey pegged crude oil inventories nationwide at 318.82 million barrels, stunning analysts expecting no more than a two million barrel build.
Crude oil imports over the past two weeks have surged above the benchmark eight million barrels, averaging 8.38 million barrels for the week ended August 23, API said.

Refiners in the key Gulf Coast refining region added a net 5.94 million barrels to inventories on hand, while West Coast refiners pumped 5.26 million net additional barrels into tank farms there, the industry trade group said.
Despite skepticism over the industry estimates and expectations the figures could be revised in next week's report, the build left traders in a bearish mood.

"It is a sign that (inventory levels) are ok but they are not as tight fundamentally, at least on the crude side, as $21 to $22 a barrel would suggest," said analyst William Brown of W.H. Brown & Co Inc.
According to API, the nation's refineries were operating at 93.8 percent of capacity last week, up 0.8 percentage points from the prior week.
U.S. refiners reported a modest, but unexpected 463,000 barrel draw in distillate stocks and a healthy, but larger than expected 2.24 million barrel draw in gasoline stocks.
Implied demand for gasoline as retailers filled storage tanks ahead of the Labor Day holiday weekend was estimated at 8.5 million barrels per day, analysts said.
The gasoline draw was fueled by refiners on the East Coast, where gasoline inventories fell 1.4 million barrels and reformulated stocks were drawn down by 2.67 million barrels, the API reported.
October crude was trading 16 cents lower at $21.40 a barrel in the ACCESS after-hours session after settling six cents lower at $21.56 a barrel in the earlier floor session.
September gasoline was 61.35 cents a gallon, up 0.14 cent in ACCESS trade after closing down 0.41 cent at 61.21 cents in the floor session.
Front-month heating oil was off 0.13 cent after-hours with sellers asking 61.15 cents a gallon. The contract closed up 0.10 cent at 61.13 cents in the floor session.
